concept.name: Transformer Self-Attention

relationships.description: Connects Transformer Self-Attention to llm prompt engineering in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Self-attention lets every token dynamically weight and aggregate information from all other tokens in a sequence in parallel, replacing sequential recurrent bottlenecks with matrix multiplications over Query, Key, and Value projections.
spark.keyTakeaway: Attention turns sequence modeling into $O(N^2 d)$ parallelizable matrix math during prefill, while autoregressive decoding shifts the bottleneck to $O(N)$ HBM memory bandwidth for reading the KV cache.

concept.whyItMatters: Modern LLMs (Llama 3, GPT-4, Claude, Gemini) rely on multi-head scaled dot-product attention to resolve long-range dependencies—like matching a closing brace or pronoun 64,000 tokens back—without vanishing gradients or sequential step-by-step recurrence.
whenToUse: Sequence-to-sequence or autoregressive tasks where tokens need direct, content-based routing across arbitrary distances (code generation, document QA, translation).
Training workloads that must saturate tensor cores on H100/TPUv5p hardware via dense GEMM operations across entire context windows in parallel.
Multi-modal fusion where cross-attention aligns disparate token spaces (e.g., ViT image patches attending to text embeddings in CLIP or Flamingo).
whenNotToUse: Ultra-long streaming telemetry or audio (>1M steps) on edge hardware where $O(N^2)$ attention matrices or multi-gigabyte KV caches exceed SRAM/DRAM budgets; prefer state-space models (Mamba-2) or 1D convolutions.
Fixed-schema tabular classification/regression (<100 features) where gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost, LightGBM) converge faster with lower inference latency and better calibration.
Hard real-time control loops (<1 ms SLA) on CPU-only embedded targets where even a small 2-layer transformer cannot meet deterministic jitter bounds.
keyPoints: Scaled dot-product attention computes $\text{softmax}(QK^T / \sqrt{d_k})V$; dividing by $\sqrt{d_k}$ (e.g., $\sqrt{128} \approx 11.31$) keeps dot-product variance at $1$ so softmax does not saturate into near-zero gradients.

Multi-Head Attention (MHA) splits $d_{\text{model}}$ (e.g., 4096) into $h$ subspaces (e.g., 32 heads of $d_k=128$) so one head tracks syntactic subject-verb agreement while another tracks coreference or positional offsets.
Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) shares Key/Value projections across groups of Query heads (e.g., 8 KV heads for 32 Q heads in Llama-3-8B), cutting KV cache memory by 4x with negligible perplexity loss.

FlashAttention-2/3 tiles $Q, K, V$ blocks inside GPU on-chip SRAM (~20 MB on H100) using online softmax, avoiding materializing the full $N \times N$ attention matrix in HBM and speeding up training 2–4x.
Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) encode relative token distance by rotating $Q$ and $K$ pairs by position-dependent angles, allowing length extrapolation via YaRN or NTK-aware scaling.

examples.title: Llama-3-70B Serving with GQA and PagedAttention
examples.scenario: A vLLM cluster serving 70B-parameter models (80 layers, 64 Q heads, 8 KV heads, $d_k=128$, FP16) handles 128 concurrent requests at 8,192 context length.
examples.outcome: With GQA (8 KV heads instead of 64), KV cache per token drops from 2.62 MB to 327 KB (2.68 GB per 8k request instead of 21.5 GB), allowing all 128 requests to fit across an 8xH100 (640 GB HBM) node with PagedAttention eliminating external fragmentation.

examples.title: Long-Context Code Repository Indexing with FlashAttention-2
examples.scenario: A code-completion model processes a 32,768-token repository context in FP16 across 32 attention heads.
examples.outcome: Standard eager attention would allocate $32 \times 32768^2 \times 2\text{ bytes} = 68.7\text{ GB}$ per layer just for the attention score matrix and OOM immediately; FlashAttention-2 keeps intermediate scores in SRAM tiles, reducing attention memory to $O(N)$ (~40 MB) and running prefill in ~1.8 seconds on an H100.

tradeOffs.pro: Every token directly attends to every prior token with zero information bottleneck.
tradeOffs.con: Prefill FLOPs scale as $O(N^2)$ and KV cache grows linearly as $O(N)$ per request, making 128k+ contexts expensive to serve at high concurrency.

tradeOffs.pro: Multi-Query (MQA, 1 KV head) and Grouped-Query (GQA) slash KV cache size and memory-bandwidth pressure during decode.
tradeOffs.con: Aggressive KV sharing (especially MQA) can degrade recall on needle-in-a-haystack or multi-hop reasoning tasks unless trained from scratch with GQA.

tradeOffs.pro: Sliding-window attention ($W=4096$, e.g., Mistral 7B) caps KV cache size at $O(W)$ regardless of total sequence length.
tradeOffs.con: Information beyond $W \times L$ hops cannot be retrieved directly, hurting exact verbatim copy tasks over long documents.

failureModes.name: KV Cache OOM and Preemption Thrashing
failureModes.description: Long-prompt bursts exhaust GPU HBM reserved for KV blocks, forcing vLLM/TGI to preempt or swap active requests to host RAM over PCIe and spiking P99 TTFT/TPOT.
failureModes.mitigation: Enable chunked prefill, enforce strict max-tokens-per-batch admission control, use FP8 KV cache quantization, and adopt GQA models.

failureModes.name: Attention Sink & Lost-in-the-Middle Degradation
failureModes.description: Models disproportionately dump unused probability mass onto the first token (BOS) and under-attend to facts buried in the middle 30–70% of a 64k+ prompt.
failureModes.mitigation: Keep BOS + recent window tokens in streaming attention (StreamingLLM), place critical instructions at the start and end of prompts, and evaluate with RULER/Needle-in-a-Haystack.

failureModes.name: Softmax Numerical Overflow / Underflow in FP16
failureModes.description: Large pre-softmax logits ($> 65504$) overflow FP16 or collapse attention weights to 0/1, producing NaN gradients during mixed-precision training.
failureModes.mitigation: Train in BF16 (8-bit exponent matching FP32 range), apply QK-Norm (RMSNorm on $Q$ and $K$ before dot product), and keep softmax accumulation in FP32.

failureModes.name: Positional Extrapolation Collapse
failureModes.description: Feeding sequences longer than the training context (e.g., 16k into a 4k RoPE model) produces unseen rotation angles, causing repetitive output garbage.
failureModes.mitigation: Apply YaRN or Dynamic NTK-aware RoPE base scaling (e.g., increasing $\theta$ from 10,000 to 500,000 as in Llama 3) and fine-tune briefly at target length.

commonMistakes: Forgetting the $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ scaling factor in custom attention kernels, which causes softmax saturation and stalled training.
Benchmarking only prefill throughput while ignoring that autoregressive token generation is HBM memory-bandwidth bound (arithmetic intensity ~1–2 FLOPs/byte at batch size 1).
Leaving causal masks unaligned with padding masks during batched training, leaking future or pad tokens into hidden states.
Assuming 128k context window means uniform retrieval accuracy across all 128k tokens without testing middle-context recall.
Computing full $N \times N$ attention matrices in PyTorch eager mode instead of calling `F.scaled_dot_product_attention` (which dispatches FlashAttention-2).

sections.content:
## The idea

In recurrent networks, token $t$ can only see token $0$ after passing through $t$ sequential hidden-state updates. Transformer self-attention removes that sequential chain. Every token embedding $x_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}}}$ is projected into three roles via learned matrices $W_Q, W_K, W_V$: a **Query** ($q_i$, what I am looking for), a **Key** ($k_i$, what I advertise), and a **Value** ($v_i$, what I contribute if matched).

For a sequence of length $N$, the attention output is:
$$\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^T + M}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V$$
where $M$ is a causal upper-triangular mask ($-\infty$ for $j > i$) in decoder-only LLMs. Scaling by $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ ensures that if $q$ and $k$ have unit variance, their dot product also has unit variance regardless of head dimension $d_k$.

## Concrete walkthrough

Consider a single head ($d_k = 128$) in Llama-3-8B processing the prompt `"The server crashed because it"` ($N=5$ tokens) during autoregressive decoding of token 6:

1. **Prefill (tokens 1–5 in parallel)**: The model multiplies the $5 \times 4096$ input matrix by $W_Q, W_K, W_V$ in one batched GEMM, producing $Q, K, V$ tensors. RoPE rotates each $q_i, k_i$ pair by angle $i \cdot \theta_m$. The $K$ and $V$ tensors for tokens 1–5 are written to the GPU KV cache.
2. **Decode step (token 6, `"it"`)**: Only the single new token embedding ($1 \times 4096$) is projected into $q_6, k_6, v_6$. $k_6$ and $v_6$ are appended to the KV cache (now length 6).
3. **Score & Aggregate**: $q_6$ is dot-multiplied against all cached keys $K_{1..6}$, yielding 6 logits. Suppose `"server"` (position 2) has the highest dot product ($4.8$ after scaling by $1/\sqrt{128}$), giving it a softmax weight of $0.76$. The output vector for `"it"` becomes $0.76 v_2 + 0.24 \sum_{j \neq 2} w_j v_j$, routing the `"server"` representation directly into the next layer's MLP.

sections.content:
## Prefill vs. decode hardware profile

Attention behaves completely differently across the two phases of LLM inference:

- **Prefill (compute-bound)**: Processing a 4,096-token prompt performs $Q K^T$ and $P V$ matrix-matrix multiplications (GEMMs) with high arithmetic intensity. On an NVIDIA H100 (989 TFLOPS FP16, 3.35 TB/s HBM3), tensor cores stay saturated.
- **Decode (memory-bandwidth-bound)**: Generating token $t+1$ uses a $1 \times d_k$ query vector against an $N \times d_k$ KV cache (GEMV). Arithmetic intensity drops near 1 FLOP/byte, meaning speed is dictated almost entirely by how fast HBM can stream the KV cache. Continuous batching and GQA directly raise effective throughput by sharing KV reads across batch items or reducing bytes fetched per head.

## Attention variants compared

| Variant | KV Heads (for 32 Q heads) | KV Cache / Token (32 layers, d_k=128, FP16) | Prefill Complexity | Typical Model |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multi-Head Attention (MHA) | 32 | 524 KB | $O(N^2 d)$ | Llama-2-7B, GPT-3 |
| Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) | 8 | 131 KB | $O(N^2 d)$ | Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B |
| Multi-Query Attention (MQA) | 1 | 16.4 KB | $O(N^2 d)$ | Falcon-40B, StarCoder |
| Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) | Compressed latent ($d_c=512$) | ~32 KB | $O(N^2 d)$ | DeepSeek-V2 / V3 |
| Sliding Window ($W=4096$) | 8 (GQA) | Capped at $4096 \times 131$ KB | $O(N W d)$ | Mistral-7B v0.1 |

## Failure modes

Production attention failures rarely look like syntax crashes—they surface as silent quality degradation or tail-latency spikes:

- **KV cache fragmentation**: Naive contiguous pre-allocation wastes 60–80% of HBM on unused max-sequence slots; PagedAttention (16-token blocks) cuts waste below 4%.
- **Context rot / needle miss**: Even when a prompt fits in 128k tokens, attention entropy rises as $N$ grows, diluting signal from relevant chunks. Hybrid retrieval (BM25 + dense vector reranking) before the prompt outperforms stuffing raw megabytes into attention.
- **Speculative decoding mismatch**: If the draft model and target verifier use different RoPE bases or causal mask edge cases, acceptance rates collapse.

## Production optimizations

Three techniques dominate high-throughput serving stacks (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM):

1. **Prefix Caching (RadixAttention)**: Shared system prompts and few-shot examples hash to the same KV blocks in a radix tree, skipping redundant prefill compute.
2. **FP8 KV Cache Quantization**: Quantizing cached $K$ and $V$ tensors to E4M3 FP8 halves HBM capacity and bandwidth demand with <0.5% accuracy drop on MMLU.
3. **Disaggregated Prefill/Decode**: Routing long-context prefill to compute-heavy nodes and decode to bandwidth-optimized nodes prevents prefill spikes from stalling streaming tokens (TPOT).

## Practical checklist

- Verify PyTorch/CUDA dispatches FlashAttention-2 or SDPA (`torch.backends.cuda.flash_sdp_enabled()`) rather than falling back to math/eager attention.
- Calculate exact KV cache footprint before sizing GPUs: `2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * bytes_per_param * seq_len * max_concurrency`.
- Train and fine-tune in BF16 with QK-Norm enabled if scaling context length or learning rate aggressively.
- Enable automatic prefix caching when >20% of requests share a system prompt or tool schema.
- Benchmark both TTFT (prefill) and TPOT (decode) at P99 under realistic concurrency, not batch-size-1 synthetic loops.

interviewProblems.title: Transformer Self-Attention
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Transformer Self-Attention. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

nodes.label: Q / K / V Projections + RoPE
nodes.role: Linear Wq, Wk, Wv & rotary phase

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Self-attention lets every token dynamically weight and aggregate information from all other tokens in a sequence in parallel, replacing sequential recurrent bottlenecks with matrix multiplications over Query, Key, and Value projections.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: SRAM Tiled Softmax applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Head Concat + W_O.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Head Concat + W_O experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Enable chunked prefill, enforce strict max-tokens-per-batch admission control, use FP8 KV cache quantization, and adopt GQA models.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Attention turns sequence modeling into $O(N^2 d)$ parallelizable matrix math during prefill, while autoregressive decoding shifts the bottleneck to $O(N)$ HBM memory bandwidth for reading the KV cache.
Avoid trap: Forgetting the $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ scaling factor in custom attention kernels, which causes softmax saturation and stalled training.
Avoid trap: Benchmarking only prefill throughput while ignoring that autoregressive token generation is HBM memory-bandwidth bound (arithmetic intensity ~1–2 FLOPs/byte at batch size 1).
When to reach for it: Sequence-to-sequence or autoregressive tasks where tokens need direct, content-based routing across arbitrary distances (code generation, document QA, translation).
When to reach for it: Training workloads that must saturate tensor cores on H100/TPUv5p hardware via dense GEMM operations across entire context windows in parallel.

putItTogether.title: Putting Transformer Attention Together
putItTogether.summary: Attention turns sequence modeling into $O(N^2 d)$ parallelizable matrix math during prefill, while autoregressive decoding shifts the bottleneck to $O(N)$ HBM memory bandwidth for reading the KV cache.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Transformer Attention before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: With GQA (8 KV heads instead of 64), KV cache per token drops from 2.62 MB to 327 KB (2.68 GB per 8k request instead of 21.5 GB), allowing all 128 requests to fit across an 8xH100 (640 GB HBM) node with PagedAttention eliminating external fragmentation.
